title: clawctl tool envelope (v1)
description: Versioned envelope shape that clawctl emitters and consumers exchange when invoking openclaw agents as typed tools. A single document is one of: ToolRequest, ToolResponse, ToolStreamChunk, ToolError. The envelope_version field MUST be '1' for every member of this family; breaking changes bump to envelope.v2.json.

EnvelopeVersion.description: Pinned literal for v1. Consumers MUST reject unknown versions rather than guessing.

AgentSlug.description: Gateway-published agent slug (e.g. 'openclaw/concierge'). Validated client-side against /v1/models when the cache is reachable; this schema only enforces shape.

Traceparent.description: W3C traceparent header value. Required on every envelope so callers can cite a trace-id (design principle 3) without dumping bodies.

SessionId.description: Optional opaque conversation handle. Servers MAY ignore it for stateless calls.

TaskId.description: Optional unit-of-work identifier, aligned with the A2A 'taskId' concept. Groups the request, its streaming chunks, and its terminal response under one task. When the caller omits it, clawctl derives a stable default from the call's trace-id so every emitted envelope still carries one. session_id (A2A 'contextId') groups multiple tasks in a conversation; task_id scopes a single call.

ToolChoice.description: Hint to the agent about whether it should call sub-tools. 'auto' is the default when omitted.

Input.description: User-provided prompt for the agent. Mirrors the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions content shape, restricted to text for v1.

content.description: Plain-text prompt. Multi-modal content (images, files) is intentionally deferred to v2.

Usage.description: Token accounting echoed from the gateway. Counts are integers; missing fields mean the gateway did not report them.

FinishReason.description: Why the agent stopped. Mirrors the OpenAI-compatible vocabulary plus 'error' for transport/agent failures surfaced inside a ToolResponse.

RedactionKind.description: Kind of secret matched by clawctl's boundary redactor. Values mirror the perl pattern table in clawctl (_redact). 'gw_token' covers literal matches against the live bearer token.

Redaction.description: One redaction event surfaced in-band so callers can detect masking without parsing stderr.

offset_hint.description: Approximate byte offset into the original (un-redacted) stdout where the match started. Diagnostic only; not authoritative.

count.description: Number of times this kind matched in the surrounding payload.

ErrorCode.description:
Stable, machine-readable error code. Mapping from gateway HTTP and curl exit codes:
  - transport.dns           -> curl 6
  - transport.connection_refused -> curl 7
  - transport.timeout       -> curl 28
  - transport.tls           -> curl 35/60
  - gateway.bad_request     -> HTTP 400
  - gateway.unauthorized    -> HTTP 401
  - gateway.forbidden       -> HTTP 403
  - gateway.not_found       -> HTTP 404
  - gateway.rate_limited    -> HTTP 429
  - gateway.internal        -> HTTP 500
  - gateway.upstream_unavailable -> HTTP 502/503/504
  - agent.unknown           -> /v1/models lookup miss or HTTP 404 with agent context
  - agent.unavailable       -> agent registered but currently disabled/draining
  - redaction.applied       -> informational; emitted alongside ToolResponse when redactions[] is non-empty and the caller asked for explicit error surfacing
  - redaction.audit_write_failed -> append to ~/.cache/clawctl/last-redaction failed
  - envelope.invalid        -> caller sent a payload that did not validate against this schema
  - usage.invalid_argument  -> caller-side argument or env-var error (clawctl exit 2)

ToolRequest.description: Caller -> clawctl. The shape an LLM emits when it wants to invoke an openclaw agent as a tool.

ToolResponse.description: clawctl -> caller. Final, non-streaming result of a tool call. 'redactions' is always present (possibly empty) so consumers can branch on it without null-checks.

output.description: Aggregate text content the agent produced, post-redaction.

ToolStreamChunk.description: clawctl -> caller. One streaming delta. The terminal frame is delivered as a ToolResponse, not a chunk; chunks always have finish_reason=null.

index.description: 0-based sequence number within this stream. Strictly increasing.

content.description: Post-redaction text fragment. May be empty (e.g. role-only frames).

redactions.description: Redactions discovered during this chunk. Buffer-aware emitters MAY hold a chunk until they can decide whether redaction is needed; see the streaming-buffering note in CLAUDE.md.

finish_reason.description: Always null for chunks; the terminal frame is emitted as a ToolResponse.

ToolError.description: clawctl -> caller. Terminal failure envelope. Maps to a non-zero clawctl exit code; see docs/transport-decisions.md for the per-subcommand contract.

message.description: Human-readable, post-redaction one-liner. Never includes secrets; bodies stay in stderr/audit.

http_status.description: Original gateway HTTP status, when the failure originated from a gateway response.

exit_code.description: clawctl exit code that accompanies this error (matches the contract documented in clawctl help).

details.description: Free-form, JSON-safe diagnostic context. Implementations MUST NOT place raw response bodies here.
